name: @khorsheed/dsh-reader
description: Link reader tab: RSS/Atom subscriptions plus pasted article links, a card feed with a readable detail view, host-side fetch and daily refresh over a Typert Remote data face

compat.notes: A page-type right-Sidebar tab (minted kind `reader`) over a Typert Remote data face. Fetching runs on the HOST, gated on the `ctx.web` seam: on the official web service feeds and pages go through the reader's own instance of the official HTTP fetch provider (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-fetch-http`, optional peer), because from 0.2.1-rc.2 the web-search settings switch can move `ctx.web` fetching to the DeepSeek Fetch API, which answers Markdown instead of the document (seam registry S22); without that package fetches go through `ctx.web.fetch`; state is written with plain `node:fs` (atomic temp+rename) under `$DSH_HOME/state/dsh-reader`, NOT through `ctx.fs` — that service is the session-fenced sandboxed filesystem, so a workspace-write session refuses a write to the state root (observed on the acceptance instance). Every optional capability is probed at apply time and degrades (no `web` → domain refusals; no `sideChat` → the side-chat gesture hides; no `quote` → selection quoting is unavailable while the entry-level quote button still works). KNOWN LIMIT: the fetch caps a decoded body at 2,000,000 chars by default (100,000 before 2026-10-27; the reader row's `fetchLimits` changes it; limits on the `web-fetch-http` row no longer reach the reader) and truncates silently, so articles larger than that cannot be extracted — the detail view falls back to a 「受限篇幅，内容未完整呈现」 notice with a 「阅读原文」 button (measured: Anthropic research pages, theverge.com, newyorker.com). On-device translation (0.2.0) runs the page's own Translator API (Chrome 138+/Edge 148+, desktop): the model never leaves the device and no model quota is spent, while the derived sentence pairs persist on the host (a global memory file plus per-entry segment maps under the state root, one shared budget, no TTL) so a reload re-paints instead of re-translating. Where that API is absent or the pair is unavailable, the globe is simply not rendered — the pane keeps working exactly as before — except that a browser without the API (iOS, Safari, Firefox) still offers the globe on a body whose stored per-entry map matches its hash, to VIEW that stored translation (no model, no retranslate). Source bodies that are already Chinese are not offered translation at all. On host 0.1.6-alpha.2+ the spots that want a real browser (the script-figure notice, a bot-wall card's action) open the in-app Sidebar Browser tab, probed through the `browser` tab kind; on older hosts they are the ordinary external link. Pages that inline real figures as base64 data URIs are now kept whole (substantive payloads over a 512-char threshold; 1px placeholders still yield to lazy-loading attributes), so a figure-heavy paper on a cap-raised deployment becomes a multi-MB cached body by design — bodies are bounded by entry count + TTL, not by a char budget. Notes (unreleased): the body highlight uses the CSS Custom Highlight API (no highlight without it, notes still work); the quote-menu 「记笔记」 row needs quote applied first, otherwise the detail foot button is the way in; 「回到会话」 needs ui-workspace's openSession; the ./tool row's reader_read / reader_note need the host tools registry and its reader skill the skills registry. The right-Sidebar tab self-hides on the ./tool row (2026-10-19, the canvas's dual check through the official pluginInventory Remote, probed): a root-mounted reader-tool row shows it everywhere, otherwise only sessions whose preset grants it (the learning and writing mode packs); every unreadable path fails open. Video and audio (unreleased): captions and channel listings run the plugin's own standalone yt-dlp on the host (fetched with curl on first use into the state root's bin/, self-updated after two weeks; ytdlpPath overrides); the YouTube embed is a frame of the plugin's own (allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-presentation) driven over postMessage; Bilibili's player reports no time (seek = reload with t); Bilibili uploader spaces and most captions need a login. Local transcription of caption-less videos and audio probes the optional `transcribe` service (@khorsheed/dsh-transcribe) per start and states its absence; the audio is fetched through yt-dlp or curl into the state root's tmp/ and deleted once transcribed.
